questions.text: Choose all the correct statements regarding compiling and linking multiple C source files using gcc
options: The command gcc file1.c file2.c -o output produces an executable named output.
The command gcc -c file1.c file2.c -o output produces an executable named output.
The command gcc -c file1.c file2.c produces file1.o and file2.o.
The command gcc file1.o file2.o -c -o output produces an executable named output.
The command gcc file1.o file2.o -o output links the object files into an executable named output.
correct_answer: The command gcc file1.c file2.c -o output produces an executable named output.
The command gcc -c file1.c file2.c produces file1.o and file2.o.
The command gcc file1.o file2.o -o output links the object files into an executable named output.

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes a key difference between the First-Come- First-Serve (FCFS) and Round Robin (RR) CPU scheduling algorithms?
options: FCFS uses a fixed time quantum, while Round Robin does not.
FCFS is non-preemptive, while Round Robin is preemptive.
Round Robin always selects the process with the shortest burst time.
Both FCFS and Round Robin are non-preemptive scheduling algorithms.
questions.correct_answer: FCFS is non-preemptive, while Round Robin is preemptive.
